title: Before Wednesday's open: inflation data and Dell's big AI quarter
text: Today is the last full trading day of the week. The market is closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and closes early on Friday. Two things to watch at the open. First, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time the government releases the PCE inflation report, the Fed's favorite way to measure rising prices, plus other data. Second, Dell reported a record quarter after Tuesday's close, with strong demand for AI servers. That could matter for chip makers like NVIDIA and AMD, which fell 5.9% and 8.9% on Tuesday. Prices in this update are from Tuesday's close.

title: Dell's results put AI hardware back in focus
text: Dell builds the big computers (servers) that run AI, and many of them use chips from companies on our list. Dell said its quarterly revenue was a record $54.9 billion, about double a year ago. It also said customers have $132.3 billion of AI orders waiting to be filled. This is a sign that spending on AI is still strong. The chip makers on our list fell much more than the big AI users on Tuesday, so watch whether this news helps them today.

title: Inflation report lands before the opening bell
text: The PCE report shows how fast prices are rising. If inflation comes in hotter than expected, the Fed may keep interest rates high or raise them, and that can push stock prices down. The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, the highest of the past 12 months. Higher interest rates tend to hit fast growing tech stocks the hardest, because their biggest profits are expected far in the future.

title: Broadcom and Rocket Lab are close to their lows of the year
text: Broadcom closed at $301.08, only about 4% above its lowest price of the past year ($289.77). Rocket Lab closed at $45.98, about 15% above its low ($39.98) and about 70% below its high. Rocket Lab's risk score is 9.9 out of 10, the highest on our list. A stock near its low is not automatically cheap. It can keep falling, so the 52 week range is a clue, not an answer.

title: Lesson 66: What is a stock buyback?
text: A buyback is when a company uses its own cash to buy back its own shares from the market. After that, there are fewer shares, so each share owns a slightly bigger slice of the company and its profits. Dell just approved up to $25 billion for buybacks. A buyback can be a sign that a company has extra cash and thinks its stock is worth owning. But it is not a promise that the price will go up. That money could also have been used to grow the business or to pay a dividend, so it is worth asking which choice helps owners more.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices, 52 week ranges, beta and company size come from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) as of Tuesday's close. Analyst price targets and company ratios come from FMP for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace; the free plan does not include them for Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly or Intuitive Surgical. The 10 year Treasury yield comes from Alpha Vantage. News comes from Dell, Kiplinger, the Associated Press, SEC filings and the NYSE. Risk scores and scenarios are simple math, not predictions. Nothing here is advice to buy or sell.
